name: Bok Choy

companions.note: Compatible brassica bed; similar pest and water needs
Radishes repel flea beetles that attack brassicas; harvest radishes as bok choy fills in

pnw_notes: One of the most productive fall brassicas in the PNW. Extremely frost-hardy — can handle temperatures into the mid-20s. Harvest whole heads at the base or take outer leaves continuously. Baby bok choy can be spaced closer at 4 in. Excellent stir-fry green; also great raw in salads when young.

frost_hardiness.notes: More frost-hardy than most brassicas. Row cover below 25°F. A light frost sweetens the flavor.

planting_windows.notes: Spring sowing; harvest before summer heat causes bolting
Fall window — best flavor; very frost-hardy
Transplant starts for fall; spacing 6 in for standard, 4 in for baby
Spring harvest; cut at base or harvest outer leaves
Fall harvest; flavor sweetens with frost
